newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha quiet, buyers and sellers at standoff.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha quiet, buyers and sellers at standoff.

text.p: NWE naphtha markets were quiet and prices talked in a wide notional range on Friday as buyers and sellers stood apart, traders said.
Despite the current overhang of prompt avails traders said relaxed buying had meant sellers were reluctant to make a market and few of the prompt cargoes were actually being shown.
Notional buyers ideas were pegged around $216-217 a tonne cif NWE while notional offers were around $220.
Cargoes of Egyptian and Algerian material, of 25-30,000 tonnes, are seen available around the end of the month, none were being offered into Europe.
They were expected to go transatlantic unless European demand picks up.
Small Russian cargoes continued to talk in a wide range with offers around mean minus $3 and bids at mean minus $10.
Sentiment for improved demand in early Jan continued to support Jan swaps prices at values around $225 a tonne.
